definition.description: REV | Intake | WordPress to Dataverse. Accepts the website's native entry (ADR-051, TAD App. C), creates the application (FR-007/008), notifies (FR-009), alerts on failure (FR-010). Duplicate check (FR-023) deferred - see notes.md.

metadata.description: Environment variable. Recipient of the FR-009 new-application notification, injected per environment at import (C-TECH-047).

Environment variable. Entra app (client) ID of the WordPress intake registration - SECOND gate only (NFR-008, C-TECH-006); primary control is the trigger's Entra auth. Public identifier, not a secret. See notes.md (client-id vs object-id).

manual.description: The one public endpoint. PRIMARY control is trigger-level Entra ID auth (NFR-008, C-TECH-006; ADR-011 decided). Native website entry body (ADR-051), hidden in run history (A-INT-01). Concurrency 1: match-or-create is read-then-write. See notes.md.

id.description: Gravity Forms entry id -> rev_application.rev_sourcesubmissionid (duplicate key only, shown to no persona). The sender MUST resend the same id on any retry.

Reject_caller_that_is_not_the_charity_we.description: NFR-008/C-TECH-006, SECOND gate only - primary control is the trigger's Entra auth. TRUE = reject: allowed id unset, or header not equal to it. 401 + Cancelled. Fails closed. Terse rejection. See notes.md.

Stop_run_unauthorised.description: Cancelled, not Failed. An unauthorised caller is not a system fault and must not raise a failure alert to the process owner - otherwise a scanner hitting the endpoint becomes a Teams notification.

Normalise_payload.description: ADR-051 item 2. The ONLY action that reads answer keys from triggerBody(): internal names per TAD App. C and C.2 type rules (A-INT-03). Not answered -> null. Over-long structured text -> null + note (ADR-053). See notes.md.

Reject_incomplete_payload.description: C-TECH-004, ADR-051 item 6. Rejects ONLY when id, name_first, name_last or address_postcode is empty - the same four facts as before, under the website's names. Nothing else rejects; a bad answer is a note. See notes.md.

Compose_run_link_for_the_rejection.description: Builds the deep link to THIS run and passes it to REV | Ops | Failure Alert. Both parts come from workflow() at run time, so nothing is hardcoded. It must be built here: workflow() in the child returns the child. See notes.md.

Log_incomplete_payload.description: FR-010. Reference only - the submission id, never the payload. Severity Warning rather than Error: the platform is healthy, the caller is not.

body.text_2: Incomplete intake payload rejected: one or more of id, name_first, name_last, address_postcode was absent or empty.

Respond_400_incomplete.description: Names the required fields so Alex can fix the integration, and returns nothing else. The applicant never sees this - Alex's specification requires the website to show a plain-English message instead.

Initialise_failure_detail.description: Holds the failed action name and reason for the alert. Declared at the TOP level: the scope that fails is skipped from the failure onward, so nothing inside it can carry a value out.

Create_the_application.description: Everything that touches Dataverse sits in one scope so a single run-after path catches every failure below it (power-automate.md: every flow has a top-level Scope with a parallel failure branch).

Find_application_with_this_submission_id.description: THE IDEMPOTENCY GUARD (TAD section 5.1). rev_sourcesubmissionid is an alternate key, so this is an indexed lookup. Runs before any write.

Return_the_existing_reference_if_this_is.description: A replayed webhook returns the original reference and writes nothing - deliberately update-free, so it can't silently overwrite a process-owner override (FR-018). Narrows TAD 5.1 - reviewer to confirm (Dev Summary D-2). See notes.md.

Stop_run_replay.description: Succeeded, not Cancelled: a correctly-handled replay is a success, and marking it Cancelled would make the run history read as though something went wrong.

Read_configuration.description: Every label/band map is read at RUN TIME from rev_setting by ONE List rows call for all 18 rows (6 + the 12 ADR-051 label maps). Never Get-a-row-by-id on an alternate key (IMP-0112). See notes.md.

Read_intake_configuration.description: FR-017/FR-027/FR-064, ADR-051 item 3. ONE List rows call for the 18 rev_setting rows this flow needs. Never Get-a-row-by-id on an alternate key (IMP-0112). See notes.md.

Compute_age_in_years.description: Exact completed years: subtract birth year, minus one more if the birthday hasn't occurred yet this year. Band boundaries matter. Returns -1 when no usable date of birth was supplied, turned into 'Not known' next. See notes.md.

Match_age_bands.description: AgeBandMap rows are held in ascending maxAge order, preserved here, so the first match is the narrowest band containing the age. Re-ordering the JSON silently degrades this - documented at both ends. See notes.md.

Map_age_range_label.description: Matches the age-range label the form sent against the configured map. Empty when no age_range was sent or the label is not in the map - the flow never guesses a band.

Derive_age_range.description: FR-084, ADR-051 item 11 (D-02). The band chosen on the form wins; else the band from a date of birth; else null - not answered. 9 (Not known) is written only when the applicant chose 'Prefer not to say'. See notes.md.

Compute_outward_code.description: The outward code is everything before the space in a UK postcode. Works for 'BT1 1AA' and for 'BT11AA' with no space, because only the leading letters are used below.

Find_local_authority_register_row.description: wbs:0.11 (CO-003). ListRows on wbs:4.6's register, filtered by alternate key = the outward code above. NEVER Get-by-id on an alternate key (IMP-0112). A-GAA-01: entity set name guessed, register table not yet built. See notes.md.

Derive_local_authority_status.description: TAD S5. No row, or register status NI Pending Licence, collapse to Not Known - same fact from the Applicant's view (S3, ADR-002). A-GAA-02: register's own option values (100001-3) are guessed, not yet buildable. See notes.md.

Derive_local_authority.description: FR-252/FR-253: null on every non-Resolved status - the register row's own rev_localauthorityname is copied only when Derive_local_authority_status resolved to 100001 (Resolved). A blank rev_localauthority is never a silent guess.

Compute_postcode_prefixes.description: Two candidates: UK postcode areas are one or two letters, and the two-letter reading must win ('BT1' -> Northern Ireland on 'BT', not West Midlands on 'B'). Logic Apps has no regex, so this fallback replaces one. See notes.md.

Derive_location_area.description: FR-027. Two-letter area wins, one-letter area is the fallback, and option 13 'Not known' is the honest answer for an unrecognised postcode. As with the age band, the flow never guesses a region.

Lookup_city_register.description: wbs:4.7 (CO-007, EF-03). ListRecords on the city register, filtered by outward code (TAD S5.2). A-CSR-01: entity set name guessed. See notes.md.

Derive_city.description: TAD S5.2. No row in the register is a miss (FR-222), not an ambiguity - this register has no resolution-status column (ADR-002). Never guesses; a miss resolves to null, exactly as Derive_location_area's own established house style never guesses a region.

Derive_intake_review_note.description: FR-064, ADR-051 item 10. The single place every non-fatal intake finding is written. Truncated to 1,990 chars plus a marker (the column holds 2,000); null when there is nothing to say.

Find_existing_applicant.description: Matches on email + name when an email was collected (only when Email is the preferred contact method); otherwise falls back to name + postcode, the only identity the form guarantees. See notes.md.

parameters.$filter: @if(empty(coalesce(outputs('Normalise_payload')?['email'], '')), concat('rev_firstname eq ''', replace(outputs('Normalise_payload')?['first_name'], '''', ''''''), ''' and rev_lastname eq ''', replace(outputs('Normalise_payload')?['last_name'], '''', ''''''), ''' and rev_postcode eq ''', replace(coalesce(outputs('Normalise_payload')?['postcode'], ''), '''', ''''''), ''''), concat('rev_email eq ''', replace(coalesce(outputs('Normalise_payload')?['email'], ''), '''', ''''''), ''' and rev_firstname eq ''', replace(outputs('Normalise_payload')?['first_name'], '''', ''''''), ''' and rev_lastname eq ''', replace(outputs('Normalise_payload')?['last_name'], '''', ''''''), ''''))

Create_or_refresh_the_applicant.description: One person, one applicant row. On a repeat application, derived columns and rev_lastcontactdate are refreshed rather than creating a second row - a stale rev_lastcontactdate would delete a live case early. See notes.md.

Refresh_existing_applicant.description: ADR-054: a question not answered this time keeps the stored value (raw-input null test; derived columns gate on their source answer). Match keys not written. rev_fullname is calculated. See notes.md.

Create_new_applicant.description: rev_name is an autonumber (REV-A-nnnnn), not set here. ADR-013: the primary name column is a pseudonymised reference. rev_privacynoticeacceptedon is not written: nobody entered it (ADR-051 item 12). See notes.md.

Resolve_applicant_id.description: One value from whichever branch ran, so the create step below has a single reference to bind to.

Create_application.description: FR-007/FR-008, ADR-051 item 12: every applicant-entered answer, nothing the form generates. rev_name autonumber; rev_status 1 Submitted; rev_submittedon = receipt time. See notes.md for the secured columns written here.

DEFERRED_call_duplicate_grant_check.description: CALL SITE PLACEHOLDER, not dead code. FR-023's QuickBooks duplicate-grant check (Automation #7) is deferred (Dev Summary section 7) - this marks the insertion point. Writes nothing. See notes.md.
DEFERRED_call_duplicate_grant_check.inputs: FR-023 duplicate check deferred to Automation #7. Insert the REV | Duplicate | QBO Check child-flow call here, passing @{outputs('Create_application')?['body/rev_applicationid']}.

Notify_process_owner_of_new_application.description: FR-009 requires the applicant NAME and reference, so unlike every other notification this one deliberately carries personal data. ADR-015: 1:1 chat to the process owner only, not a channel. See notes.md.

parameters.body/messageBody:
New grant application received

Applicant: @{concat(outputs('Normalise_payload')?['first_name'], ' ', outputs('Normalise_payload')?['last_name'])}
Reference: @{outputs('Create_application')?['body/rev_name']}
Received: @{formatDateTime(outputs('Normalise_payload')?['received_at'], 'dd MMM yyyy HH:mm')} UTC

Scoring runs automatically. You will be notified again only if this application comes out Borderline or if a scored answer was missing.

Respond_201_created.description: Responds success even if the Teams notification failed: the application record exists, so the submission succeeded, and an error here would make the site retry and alarm the applicant for nothing. See notes.md.

Find_the_failed_action.description: The child of the failed scope whose status is Failed. result(scope)[0] was used before and returns the FIRST child, whose message on a nested scope is a generic wrapper - 11 alerts once said only "An action failed".

Describe_the_failure.description: When the failed child is the nested Read_configuration scope, descend to the action that actually failed - result() on a scope gives a generic wrapper message (IMP-0109). Otherwise the outer child IS the leaf. See notes.md.

Find_the_failed_step_inside_Read_configu.description: Only evaluated when Read_configuration is the failure, so result() on it is safe.

Set_failure_detail_from_the_nested_scope.description: The leaf action inside the nested scope - the one with the real message.

inputs.name: failureDetail
inputs.value: @{concat('Action: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_step_inside_Read_configuration'))?['name'], 'unknown'), ' | Code: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_step_inside_Read_configuration'))?['error']?['code'], 'none'), ' | Reason: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_step_inside_Read_configuration'))?['error']?['message'], 'no message supplied by the platform'))}

Set_failure_detail.description: The failed child was not a scope, so it is already the leaf.

inputs.name: failureDetail
inputs.value: @{concat('Action: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_action'))?['name'], 'unknown'), ' | Code: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_action'))?['error']?['code'], 'none'), ' | Reason: ', coalesce(first(body('Find_the_failed_action'))?['error']?['message'], 'no message supplied by the platform'))}

Compose_run_link.description: Builds the deep link to THIS run and passes it to REV | Ops | Failure Alert. Both parts come from workflow() at run time, so nothing is hardcoded. It must be built here: workflow() in the child returns the child. See notes.md.

Alert_on_failure.description: FR-010: no submission is silently lost. Passes only the submission id as the record reference so it can be identified and re-sent - nothing else from the payload, which carries special-category data (NFR-012, C-DOM-004).

Respond_500_intake_failed.description: Tells the site to retry with the SAME entry id - safe due to the idempotency guard above. Returns no diagnostic detail: the applicant must never see a raw error, nor the endpoint its internals to an unauthenticated caller.

body.guidance: Retry with the same entry id. Duplicate submissions are rejected safely.
